I will still do wheat-maize on the full 4.1 mu, same as before. On my land here in Quzhou, if I stop changing things too much and keep water and fertilizer in place, the harvest is steadier. I have only 4.1 mu, so every bag of fertilizer costs real money, but if I cut too hard and the yield drops, that loss hurts more than a little extra fertilizer. I usually look at what works around me, and around here the better fields all feed wheat heavier than maize, because wheat needs a stronger base and good spring growth.

For wheat, I will use improved seed, not old saved seed. I have seen the newer kinds stand better and fill grain better if water keeps up. I will put more nitrogen on wheat than maize, and I will not leave out phosphorus because our area responds to base fertilizer. Potash I will use, but not too heavy, just enough to keep stalks and grain stronger. Since I have well irrigation, I will give wheat three waters if the season is normal: one after sowing or for overwintering if needed, one at jointing, and one around grain filling. If disease and aphids show up, I will spray twice. I will rotary till after the maize season because on a small plot that is simpler and cheaper than deeper ploughing every time.

For maize, I will also use hybrid seed. Around here, hybrid maize is the normal way now, and I have seen it outyield the older seed. I will not feed maize as heavily as wheat at the start, but I will still give enough nitrogen because if maize goes pale in summer, yield falls fast. With well water, I can manage two irrigations in a normal year, mainly around big jointing and silking if rain is short. For weeds, borers, and leaf disease, I will plan on two pesticide applications. If the summer rains are decent, I should still get a solid maize crop on this land.
